# Data audit (generated by `python -m src.audit`)

## 1. Panel structure

- train 1494 rows, test 654 rows; 1216 distinct days; 29 independent numeric variables
- `FR_DE_EXCHANGE` = -`DE_FR_EXCHANGE` exactly (max abs sum 0.0e+00): dropped
- `DE_NET_IMPORT` = -`DE_NET_EXPORT` exactly (max abs sum 0.0e+00): dropped
- `FR_NET_IMPORT` = -`FR_NET_EXPORT` exactly (max abs sum 0.0e+00): dropped
- rows per day: {'DE+FR': 932, 'FR': 284} (every day has an FR row; DE is missing on some days)
- explanatory variables of the FR and DE rows of a day are identical (max difference 0.0e+00)
- no day is shared between train and test: 0 common DAY_ID

## 2. Chronology: `ID` is ordered in time, `DAY_ID` is not

- ID ranges: DE 0-931, FR 932-2147
| variable         |   lag-1 autocorr, DAY_ID order |   lag-1 autocorr, ID order |
|:-----------------|-------------------------------:|---------------------------:|
| FR_NUCLEAR       |                         -0.004 |                      0.98  |
| FR_CONSUMPTION   |                          0.002 |                      0.965 |
| DE_SOLAR         |                         -0.013 |                      0.882 |
| DE_TEMP          |                          0.019 |                      0.737 |
| DE_WINDPOW       |                         -0.015 |                      0.632 |
| DE_RESIDUAL_LOAD |                          0.008 |                      0.578 |
| GAS_RET          |                         -0.016 |                      0.18  |

- the DE block sorted by ID visits the days in the same order as the FR block: True
- so t = rank of the FR row's ID is a time axis for all 1,216 days (`src/data.py`).
- no weekly cycle: t mod 5 or 7 explains under 1% of the variance of consumption changes, so t is ordinal, not a calendar.
- test days are interleaved with train days at random: 527 train/test alternations along time, 511 expected under random mixing; test share per time decile [0.3, 0.25, 0.3, 0.3, 0.25, 0.37, 0.29, 0.28, 0.39, 0.27]
- DE rows exist for every day from t = 284 onwards (932 days, no gap: True); before that the panel is FR only
